solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: CID authorise cell to get Kitty banged up. Snooping did for her

indicators.note: banged up means battered and knocked about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Detectives get permission to lock a woman called Kitty in a cell; her nosiness proved her undoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banged up' looks like prison slang for locking Kitty away, but it signals a rearrangement of all the letters of CID AUTHORISE CELL plus KITTY.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns that nosiness brings ruin, and here the feline it names is a 'her' undone by her prying.

clue.text: See 19
Suspend girl who's out of practice, we've heard

indicators.note: we've heard says the words are spoken, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a girl out of practice is rusty, and Kate is a girl's name: Rusty Kate

explanation.surface: A girl who has let her skills slip is to be suspended, so the rumour goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Universities, especially Oxford and Cambridge, use this verb for sending a student away temporarily as a punishment.

clue.text: Miner loses credit for snowboard jump

indicators.note: loses says letters are taken away from the miner's word

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner
CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts

explanation.surface: A coal miner swaps his credit for a trick on a snowboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The C and R come out of COLLIER from separate places, the first letter and the last.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for a jump where the rider pops the board into the air without grabbing it, borrowed from skateboarding.

clue.text: Cast out unsanctioned organisation over slur

indicators.note: out says the letters of the word cast are thrown out of the longer word
organisation means arranging, so the remaining letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the four letters of cast, taken as written

explanation.surface: Expel an unofficial body for insulting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C, A, S, T from UNSANCTIONED to leave UNNIONED, and 'organisation' rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are an indirect remark that hints at something discreditable, a veiled insinuation rather than an open accusation.

clue.text: Funny man's only appearance is from beyond the grave

definitions.text: Funny man's only appearance is from beyond the grave

parts.words: Funny man's only appearance is from beyond the grave
parts.note: in Hamlet the king's late jester is seen only as a skull dug up in the graveyard scene

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's jester is already dead in Hamlet; the prince holds his skull and recalls him as 'a fellow of infinite jest'.

clue.text: One has attraction to a model raised, but there's no hope

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the run of pieces is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: pull means attraction or appeal
to sit is to pose as a model for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone is drawn to a fashion model, but the romance is hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' works because this is a down clue: the three pieces are read upwards, and 'to' and 'has' are only link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says the game is over and nothing can be saved, as in a situation beyond hope.

clue.text: Poorest laptop allocated to contract partner

parts.note: the top of the word lap is its first letter, L
in contract bridge the players sit as compass points, and East is West's partner

explanation.surface: The worst laptop was given to a partner on a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' is the bridge game, not a legal agreement; bridge partners are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative meaning smallest in amount or importance can stand for lowest in quality, the most meagre.

clue.text: Fearsome lecturer's not finished infiltrating payment mechanism

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the shortened lecturer goes within the payment letters

parts.note: DD stands for direct debit, a way of paying bills automatically

indicators.note: not finished says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a reader is a senior university lecturer in the UK

explanation.surface: An academic, mid-sentence, worms his way into a payment system to frightening effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' trims the last letter; in British universities a Reader is a senior academic ranking just below professor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something feared intensely is terrifying, so the past participle works as an adjective for frightening.

clue.text: Sugar production regulator?

parts.note: reads like an official overseeing a sugar industry, but means the hormone that controls blood glucose

explanation.definitionFit: This pancreatic hormone controls the level of glucose in the blood, so it regulates the body's handling of sugar.

clue.text: Cereal as requested by spectators in Surrey

indicators.note: as requested suggests the word as it is asked for out loud, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: rye is a cereal grain
the gate is the number of spectators attending a match

explanation.surface: Fans in Surrey asked for a particular breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south of London; this town in it is pronounced like RYE.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is a commuter settlement located in the county south of London, so it is a place in that county.

clue.text: Perhaps Stanley has potassium, nickel and iron amalgam

parts.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Someone called Stanley owns an alloy of three metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amalgam' just sums up the three symbols joined together; it is not a rearrangement signal. 'Stanley' is a brand of utility blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stanley is a retractable utility cutting tool, so it is an example of a blade, flagged by 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Magical French singer foregoes exercise in finale

indicators.note: in says the shortened singer goes inside the finale word

parts.note: a finale is the end

indicators.note: foregoes means gives up, so the exercise word is dropped from the singer

parts.note: a chanteuse is a female singer, a word borrowed from French
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A French singer skips her workout at the climax of a magical show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foregoes' drops the exercise word from the singer, and 'in' puts what is left inside the finale word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something under a spell is bewitched, which is what magical means here.

clue.text: Approach inventor who's returning, not on the left in UK

parts.note: to approach is to near

indicators.note: returning means the inventor's name is read backwards
not says the word on is dropped

parts.note: Thomas Edison was the inventor of the light bulb and phonograph

explanation.surface: Approach a returning inventor, but not on the left-hand side in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: EDISON without ON is EDIS, and 'returning' reads it backwards as SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain cars drive on the left, so the side of a vehicle nearest the kerb is the left-hand side.

clue.text: Group that sees no reason to change

definitions.text: Group that sees no reason to change

parts.words: Group that sees no reason to change
parts.note: the rock band whose name is Latin for the existing state of affairs, which by definition does not change

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the existing arrangement, and it is also the name of a long-running British rock band.

clue.text: Tranquil lake

definitions.meaning: Lake ... is a lake and resort in New York State, host of two Winter Olympics

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means calm and unruffled, and it also names a lake in the Adirondacks.

clue.text: Coming to hold on to one guy in the middle

indicators.note: in the middle says the two pieces go within the word for holding on

parts.note: to cling is to grip tightly
one is the Roman numeral I
Max is a man's name

explanation.surface: A clingy embrace around a man at the centre of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching the peak or culmination of something is arriving at its high point, here arriving in a sexual sense.

clue.text: Activity that requires guarantee to be prepared

parts.note: to give your word is to guarantee something
game means willing or prepared

explanation.surface: A task that needs a promise before you are ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble, crosswords and similar puzzles are a pastime played with vocabulary, so they count as an activity.

clue.text: See 1
Flat outside is in a bad way

indicators.note: in a bad way means in a poor state, so the letters are put in disorder

explanation.surface: The exterior of an apartment is in poor condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a home, but it is the definition; the seven letters of OUTSIDE are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of dull and lifeless matches boring and wearisome.

clue.text: Ageing boiler has run out of water?

definitions.meaning: no longer young, past one's prime

definitions.text: boiler has run out of water?
definitions.meaning: a boiler is an older bird for the pot, and a spring is a water source, so this boiler has none

explanation.walkthrough: 'boiler' looks like a water heater, but it is a fowl old enough to need boiling rather than roasting.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone no longer young, and read literally it is a bird without a source of water.

clue.text: Meaningful look clearing before six months?

parts.note: a glade is a clearing in a wood
six months is half a year, so half of the word year: its first two letters

explanation.surface: A woodland opening seen half a year ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: This old phrase means a flirtatious or amorous glance, a look full of meaning.

clue.text: Risk comes at that point where umpire finally stands down

indicators.note: stands down means withdraws, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: thereat is an old word meaning at that place or at that time

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of umpire

explanation.surface: Danger arises at the moment the umpire finally retires.
explanation.definitionFit: A danger or menace is a hazard, so a possible source of harm is a risk.

clue.text: Abandoned gel craved university admission

parts.note: gel is the posh pronunciation of girl, and a deb is a debutante, a society girl

indicators.note: admission means letting in, so the university letter is let into the craving word

parts.note: ached means longed or craved

explanation.surface: A girl longed to get into university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gel' is the upper-class British pronunciation of 'girl', and a deb is a debutante.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned in the moral sense means wild and dissolute, given over to vice.

clue.text: Commit laboratory to return a little of the dish …

indicators.note: to return says the hidden letters are read backwards
a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Run on into the next clue: send a sample from the lab back with some food.
explanation.definitionFit: A Birmingham-style curry cooked and served in a small two-handled metal pan is this dish.

clue.text: Show a change from 25th to 26th at the Mall

indicators.note: change from ... to says one letter of the show is swapped for another

parts.note: a play is a show
Y is the 25th letter of the alphabet
Z is the 26th letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A performance moves from one date to the next at a shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: '25th' and '26th' look like dates but are letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An open public square or shopping precinct, which in North America often means a mall.

clue.text: … of selected canapes tonight. Such sauce!

indicators.note: selected says a run of letters is picked out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a dish and some chosen nibbles this evening, with a cheeky exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across canaPES TOnight; 'Such sauce!' doubles as a cry at cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genoese basil, pine nut and parmesan paste is served as a sauce for pasta.

clue.text: Inclined to be devious

explanation.definitionFit: The word means slanting or sloping, and also indirect or evasive in manner.

clue.text: A unique selling point launches one church's sign

indicators.note: launches means starts off, so the first pieces come before what follows

parts.note: USP is the marketing abbreviation for unique selling point
one is the Roman numeral I
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A marketing gimmick kicks off one church's new signage.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen or portent, especially from watching birds in ancient Rome, is a sign of what is to come.

clue.text: Footling upset he passed off as minor mistake

indicators.note: passed off means disguised as something else, so the letters are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone dismissed a trivial upset as a small error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the rearrangement signal but is part of the letters; all fifteen of FOOTLING UPSET HE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A small verbal blunder is saying the wrong word by accident, which is a minor error.
